blocks.content: The Central Bureau of Investigation is the premier investigating agency of India and plays a main role in prevention of corruption and maintaining integrity in administration.

items: CBI is NOT a statutory body; it was created by an executive resolution and derives power from the DSPE Act, 1946.
The recommendation for the establishment of CBI was made by the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption.
CBI acts as the National Central Bureau of INTERPOL in India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The CBI was set up in 1963 by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
It is not a statutory body; it derives its investigative powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) Act, 1946.
The CBI functions under the administrative control of the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT), Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.
It investigates cases of corruption, economic offenses, special crimes, and handles international police cooperation as India's Interpol nodal agency.
